title: Men's afro hair: waves, fades, durags and the nape
question_forms: How do I get and keep waves, a fade or a durag routine?
How do I care for 4c hair as a man?
tradition_says: Waves are trained by brushing in a pattern, moisturising several times a day and wearing a durag at night. Close fades and tapers are kept sharp with regular cuts, and men are told 4c hair needs little care.

layer1.plain_answer: No study has tested a waves routine or durags for scalp or hair health. Barber guides say brush, moisturise and wear a satin durag; that is untested. The part with a medical record is the nape: bumps from very close cuts or shaving there can be acne keloidalis nuchae, a scarring condition in men of African descent.

do.text: Start with a healthy scalp: treat dryness or dandruff before a brushing routine.

source.name: Wise Barber, "How to get 360 waves" (a barber guide site)

do.text: Wear a silk or satin durag at night, with the seam outside and not tied too tight.

source.name: Wise Barber, "How to get 360 waves" (a barber guide site)

do.text: Use a soft brush if the scalp is sensitive.

source.name: Wise Barber, "How to get 360 waves" (a barber guide site)

do.text: Wash 4c hair every 1 to 3 weeks and use conditioner, as for any coiled hair.

source.name: British Association of Dermatologists, patient leaflet "Caring for Afro-textured hair" (July 2023)

do.text: See a doctor for bumps at the back of the neck: acne keloidalis nuchae is a scarring condition.

avoid.text: Brushing hard or three times a day on a tender scalp: hard bristles can be harsh.

source.name: Wise Barber, "How to get 360 waves" (a barber guide site)

avoid.text: Tying a durag or head wrap so tight it pulls.

source.name: British Association of Dermatologists, patient leaflet "Traction alopecia"

avoid.text: Ignoring bumps, pus or keloid-like scars at the nape; very close cuts there are suspected, not proven, triggers.

see_someone_when: Bumps, pus or scars at the back of the head or neck (doctor, then dermatologist: acne keloidalis nuchae).
Itchy, flaky scalp that has not settled after 4 weeks of an anti-dandruff shampoo (doctor).
Hairline thinning, crown thinning or tenderness (dermatologist).

tested.population: Review of acne keloidalis nuchae (folliculitis keloidalis nuchae)
tested.finding: AKN is a chronic scarring folliculitis seen mostly in men of African descent after puberty and is classed as a primary scarring alopecia. The cause is unknown; suggested inciting factors include androgens, inflammation, infection, trauma, genetics and ingrowing hairs.

tested.design: Prevalence survey of clean-shave haircut bleeding and folliculitis keloidalis nuchae
tested.finding: Haircut-associated bleeding and FKN were studied in men who wear the very close "chiskop" haircut; FKN prevalence was similar to published population data. The abstract is truncated beyond that in the record read.
tested.note: Only the first part of the abstract was read; the bleeding result is not quoted.

tested.design: PubMed search run 12 Nov 2026, exact string: (durag OR "360 waves" OR "hair brushing" OR pomade) AND (scalp OR hair) AND (African American OR Black OR afro) (result count 5).
tested.finding: My search found nothing relevant: the string returned 5 results: a stroke motion-capture paper, a breast cancer and puberty product-use cohort, an acne review, a sheep paper and a 1995 review of skin disorders in Black children (PMIDs 42973162, 38306193, 34818170, 29037398, 7742234); none studies waves routines or durags. Control: PubMed search "Khumalo NP AND hair" returned 71 results on the same day. Earlier note kept: My search found nothing: no study of waves routines or durags and scalp or hair health.

tier_driver: That a waves routine or durag helps or harms the scalp: no study found; barber guides are commercial advice.
tier_note: D because the claims about waves and durags have no human study. The nape condition (acne keloidalis nuchae) is B evidence from reviews and is cited as a harm signal. A study of scalp outcomes by grooming practice would move it.
harm_note: Acne keloidalis nuchae is a chronic scarring folliculitis seen mostly in men of African descent, causes unknown with trauma and ingrowing hairs suggested (Ogunbiyi 2016). Close cuts are suspected, not proven.
evidence_summary: A review of acne keloidalis nuchae (Ogunbiyi 2016) describes it as chronic scarring folliculitis mostly in post-pubertal men of African descent, with androgens, inflammation, infection, trauma, genetics and ingrowing hairs suggested but the cause unknown. A South African survey of men wearing a very close clean-shave haircut (the "chiskop") looked at haircut-associated bleeding and nape keloids (Khumalo 2013; only the opening of the abstract was read). The waves routine advice (brush daily, moisturise three times a day, wear a durag) is from a barber guide site and is untested.
gaps: Untested: any waves routine, durag, brushing or pomade on scalp health; whether close fades cause nape bumps (suspected only); men's braid care (see the braids entry). No men-specific wash-interval study.
